<!-- docs-drift-check -->
### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **2** package(s): `@objectstack/runtime`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **16** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **2** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/api-surface/contracts.json`, `packages/spec/export-origins/contracts.json`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**47** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json e4a16d05e84d62895a6e3f8d77ab093f7417dba0`.

⛔ **12** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **2** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/api-surface/contracts.json`, `packages/spec/export-origins/contracts.json`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **1** cross-cutting symbol(s) contributed no route anchor: `userId (5 routes)`
- **3** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **178** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json e4a16d05e84d62895a6e3f8d77ab093f7417dba0` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `5e71cbaf1859306068f82511b6868c81208e19cc` — the merge of head `16f04a5fbdb3e6c84472dd5d6f00c04a429a2949` into base `e4a16d05e84d62895a6e3f8d77ab093f7417dba0`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 5e71cbaf1859306068f82511b6868c81208e19cc && git checkout 5e71cbaf1859306068f82511b6868c81208e19cc
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin e4a16d05e84d62895a6e3f8d77ab093f7417dba0 16f04a5fbdb3e6c84472dd5d6f00c04a429a2949 && git checkout -B drift-repro e4a16d05e84d62895a6e3f8d77ab093f7417dba0 && git merge --no-ff 16f04a5fbdb3e6c84472dd5d6f00c04a429a2949

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json e4a16d05e84d62895a6e3f8d77ab093f7417dba0
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs e4a16d05e84d62895a6e3f8d77ab093f7417dba0` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## 席位核对

**L1 first review (full) · ACCEPT (one nit)** · Head-sha: `30f7347df0539e8fe0e56fcd21c93c9827e9c9a4` · card #34184 (`Fixes #34184`) · read 2026-11-17T13:30Z

There is no earlier L1 or contract-review record on any head. Inputs:
- claim 6943289412, ruling 6942875153 (Q1 A, Q2 A), hand-off 6948356800, takeover 6949051710;
- the PR body;
- the net diff from merge-base `dc66d330` (8 files, +354 / -7);
- check-runs on this head.

**Scope reading.** This is not security behaviour. No authorization decision moves. `req.user.id` stays the impersonated user, and nothing on the platform reads the two new keys. They are facts handed to AI route handlers for a later door to judge, which is what ruling Q2 A says ("carried to the gate unchanged; the gate judges it"). The card is `enhancement`. It carries no `security` label.

### Nit

- **N1.** `ai.ts` trims `ec.impersonatedBy` (`typeof … === 'string' ? ec.impersonatedBy.trim() : ''`), and a blank value adds no key. The changeset, the `AIRouteUser.impersonatedBy` doc and the code comment all say "carried as is". The value is a `sys_user` id, so trimming changes nothing real, and dropping a blank value is the right call; the pin `a blank impersonatedBy adds no key` covers it. Only the words disagree: either say "a blank value is absent" in those three places, or drop the trim. Under the small-flaw rule this does not block. It becomes its own card if it is not folded in before landing.

### Checklist

- **Surface:** all 8 paths are inside claim 6943289412: `ai.ts`, the new test, `admitting-credential.ts`, `ai-service.ts`, the two generated spec files, the new changeset, and the declared correction of the pending `33808` note.
- **Declarations:** `Clause-②: yes` matches the diff. `AIRouteUser` and `AIRouteCredentialKind` are new exports of `@objectstack/spec/contracts`, and the `api-surface` and `export-origins` rows match them exactly. `Metadata-protocol: none` is right, since nothing authorable moves, so `patch` for spec and runtime follows the level rule. Both lines are in the body and in the changeset.
- **DELIBERATE CORRECTION of `.changeset/33808-ai-door-confirmation-in-app.md`: confirmed by this ACCEPT.** The old FROM/TO line listed "bearer token" among the credentials the in-app door refuses. Under Q1 A, a session token in an `Authorization: Bearer` header is the person's session, so that sentence would ship false. The new line ("an API key, an OAuth token or another service credential … whether its session token rides in the cookie or in an `Authorization: Bearer` header") matches the ruling and `admittingCredentialKind`. The PR body declares it and quotes both sentences. `Check Changeset` is red on this head by design for this edit, and it is the only red check (latest attempt per check, 67 checks).
- **Code:**
  - `credential` is the one reading `admittingCredentialKind` already gives the membership gate. `oauth` wins on `oauthScopes`, else the admission's `api_key` or `session`, else absent.
  - `AdmittingCredentialKind` now aliases the spec type, so the gate and the door cannot spell a value two ways.
  - Both keys are absent, never `undefined`, when there is nothing to say.
  - The anonymous path (`user` absent) is unchanged.
  - `actorUserFromExecutionContext` still builds the rest, so existing keys keep their values.
- **Tests:** six cases go through `dispatch()` with the dispatcher's own identity step, behind a stub auth service that reads one session per token from either carrier:
  - a cookie session;
  - an impersonated session;
  - an API key;
  - an API key beside an impersonated cookie (`api_key`, no `impersonatedBy`, which is right because the key admitted the call);
  - a bearer-carried session;
  - an impersonated bearer session.

  Three handler-level cases cover OAuth scopes, no admission and a blank `impersonatedBy`.
- **Docs made false:** none found, beyond N1's wording.

**Owed, for the seat:** a contract review at CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER. It is owed for the two new public exports of `@objectstack/spec/contracts` (non-test `packages/spec/src/**`). On Tier H: the hand-off says "Tier H ①–④ with os-zhuang's approval", but `check-governed-merges.mjs --pr 34736` reads NOT governed (0 of 8 paths, 361 lines). Please settle which applies, as you did on #34811. This comment readies, queues and arms nothing.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `30f7347df0539e8fe0e56fcd21c93c9827e9c9a4`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/contracts/ai-service.ts + packages/runtime/src/domains/ai.ts, packages/runtime/src/security/admitting-credential.ts

First contract review of PR #34736 (card #34184). Read: the card body and all seven comments (seat analysis 6931424442, ruling 6942875153, claim 6943289412, dev report 6944692301, hand-off 6948356800, takeover 6949051710), the PR body, the eight-file list, the net diff against `main` (merge base `dc66d3308271`), and the 71 check-runs on the head. Code outside the diff was read at the head, never reviewed: `core/src/security/resolve-authz-context.ts`, `request-execution-context.ts`, `assemble-execution-context.ts`, `anonymous-deny.ts`, `runtime/src/http-dispatcher.ts`, `runtime/src/security/resolve-execution-context.ts`, `actor-user.ts`, `action-execution.ts`, `spec/src/identity/eval-user.zod.ts`, `spec/src/kernel/execution-context.zod.ts`. The remainder of the diff (the new test file, the two changesets, `api-surface/contracts.json`, `export-origins/contracts.json`) is the lane seat's ACCEPT at `TIER_DEFAULT`; the 33808 changeset sentence is judged below only because the brief asks for it and the foreign-changeset gate names this record as its confirmer.

### ① Derived judgments

- Public surface, `@objectstack/spec/contracts`: two new type-only exports, `AIRouteCredentialKind` (type) and `AIRouteUser` (interface). Right. Both are additive; `api-surface/contracts.json` and `export-origins/contracts.json` each gain exactly these two rows and nothing else moves. No existing export, signature or schema changes. The new `import type { EvalUser }` from `../identity/eval-user.zod.js` is type-only, so it adds no runtime edge between the contracts and identity entries.
- Accept-set of `AIRouteCredentialKind`: `session | api_key | oauth`. Right. It is byte for byte the set runtime's `AdmittingCredentialKind` had on `main`, and it is ruling 6942875153 Q1 A. Runtime's type is now an alias of the spec's, so the membership gate (`http-dispatcher.ts:1808`), the api-action forward (`action-execution.ts:1673, 1762`) and the AI route spell one vocabulary; the alias changes no value any of the three produces.
- `req.user` on an AI route: two new optional keys, every pre-existing key and value unchanged (`{ ...actor, ... }` over the same `actorUserFromExecutionContext` call). Right, and additive for every existing handler. `/actions` and MCP `run_action` do not pass through this literal and are untouched.
- Security reading (the brief's question on L1-e): CONFIRMED that the `impersonatedBy` carriage is not security behaviour in this PR. Reasons, from the tree: (a) no authorization decision in this repository reads the new key. The only writer is the `req.user` literal in `domains/ai.ts`, and no route, gate or middleware in the diff or the tree branches on `req.user.impersonatedBy` or `req.user.credential`; (b) the subject does not move, `id` and every grant channel stay the impersonated user's; (c) nothing new crosses a trust boundary. The value is `ExecutionContext.impersonatedBy`, server-constructed off the session read (`resolve-authz-context.ts:692-693, 721`), handed to in-process route handlers that already receive `headers` whole; it is not put on any response; (d) the direction a consumer can move with it is refusal only, which is Q2 A as ruled. What it is: a security-relevant CONTRACT, since a person-only door will rest a refusal on it. That is why ④ tests its fail-closed properties rather than waving it through, and they hold.
- `ExecutionContext.impersonatedBy`'s own description is unchanged ("ATTRIBUTION ONLY — no security middleware reads it"). Right under Q2 A, and still true after this PR: the platform's middleware does not read it; the consuming door is outside the platform's authorization path.

### ② Semver level

Clause-②: yes — matches the tree: the diff widens the published surface by two exports and narrows nothing. The takeover claim's `yes (widening)` is the same arm.

`.changeset/34184-ai-route-user-credential.md` declares `@objectstack/spec: patch`, `@objectstack/runtime: patch`, `Metadata-protocol: none`. Right. No metadata author can write anything new (a TypeScript contract type and a runtime field, no schema key, no accepted value), so the kind is `none`, and AGENTS.md rule 3 gives `none` a `patch`, a non-protocol widening included. Both packages the diff moves are named. No BREAKING banner is owed and none is carried.

Check Changeset (red, two runs: 133952505706, 133958977656). Two questions:

- Does it block the merge queue? No. The active ruleset on `main` (12119582) requires eleven contexts: TypeScript Type Check, Test Core, Build Core, Lint & Repo Gates, Governed Surface Queue Guard, Lint UI, Build & E2E UI, Type Check UI, Test UI, Live E2E UI, Dogfood Regression Gate. `Check Changeset` is not among them. On this head ten of the eleven are `success` and `Lint UI` is `skipped` by its path filter. The red check is advisory to the queue; what it demands is a confirming record, which is this one.
- Is the correction right? Yes. The gate's finding is rule 2 (the foreign-changeset rule), DELIBERATE CORRECTION class, and the PR body declares it by name with both sentences quoted. The old sentence listed "an API key or bearer token" as the credentials the in-app approve and reject doors stop taking. Under Q1 A a session whose token rides in `Authorization: Bearer` is the person's signed-in session, so that sentence, once this PR lands, would tell a split-origin Console user that their own session is refused: false. The new sentence ("an API key, an OAuth token or another service credential TO the person's signed-in session to the app, whether its session token rides in the cookie or in an `Authorization: Bearer` header") agrees with the contract prose already on `main` in the same file (`AI_ACTION_CONFIRMATION_CAPABILITY` rule 4, "an API key, a delegated or OAuth token and any other service credential"; lines 543, 594-595, 1002-1003), with the semantic entry `in-app-pending-action-decided-by-person` ("an API key, a token or an AI ..."), and with the seat's execution note under the ruling. It widens nothing the 33808 narrowing declared: that changeset's `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` line, its frontmatter and every other line are untouched, and a bearer-carried session was never a "service credential" in the contract text. This same-head at-tier PASS is the confirmation the gate's remedy names; restoring the base text would put the false sentence back.
- Residual, as the PR states: if Version Packages #33849 ships first, the old sentence goes out and the correction becomes a docs-only amend. Not a finding on this head.

### ③ Boundary flags

- Dev `open_questions` (report 6944692301): "Contract review owed ... route to the L2 review seat at head 30f7347df0". Answered by this record, on that head.
- Dev flag, not filed: `AIRouteUser` re-declares the key set runtime's `ActorUser` declares; a key added to `ActorUser` alone is not caught. Answered: accepted. The typed assignment `user: AIRouteUser = { ...actor, ... }` makes the compiler refuse the dangerous direction (a key the spec promises that runtime stops producing). The uncaught direction publishes an undeclared extra key, which contradicts nothing in the contract. Follow-up card at most; see N3.
- Dev flag, not filed: "token" wording left as is in the semantic entry, `.changeset/34189-pending-action-decide-session.md` and the `rejectPendingAction` docblock. Answered: accepted. Read at the head, each says "token" beside "API key" and "service credential", never "bearer"; under Q1 A they read as OAuth or service tokens and none states that a bearer-carried session is refused.
- Dev deviation (two read-only `gh` calls): no effect on the diff. The lane seat's.
- Takeover flag (6949051710): "If L1 reads the `impersonatedBy` carriage as security behaviour, it goes to the seat". Answered in ①: it is not, with reasons.
- Hand-off flag (6948356800): the DELIBERATE CORRECTION needs its confirming record. Answered in ②.
- SQL push-down: no finding. The diff adds no query, no id materialisation and no in-app join. Both new values are read off facts the identity step already resolved for the request (`ec.impersonatedBy`, `context.admission`, `ec.oauthScopes`); the one `sys_user` read on this path (`resolveActorDisplayName`) predates the PR and is unchanged.

### ④ Design judgment

No must-fix, no should-fix.

`packages/spec/src/contracts/ai-service.ts`, against ruling 6942875153 and its first consumer (the cloud pending-action door that must admit only the person, on their own session):

- `session` "whichever carrier brought its token ... the same session, read by the same session read". Holds. `resolveAuthzContext` has one session arm (`resolve-authz-context.ts:681-697`) that calls `getSession(headers)` once and sets `credential = 'session'`; the carrier is the auth service's business and is never recorded. Q1 A exactly.
- `api_key` precedence. Holds, and it is the property the consumer needs: a key outranks the session and a refused, held or lifecycle-dead key never falls through to the cookie beside it (`:618-679`), so `impersonatedBy` is set only on the session arm and a key beside an impersonated cookie reports `api_key` with no `impersonatedBy`. The diff's test pins that case.
- `oauth`. Holds. An OAuth access token is honoured on the MCP path alone (`http-dispatcher.ts` `acceptOAuthAccessToken`), so on an AI route `oauth` arises only from the in-process forward: `resolve-execution-context.ts:187-194` redeems the forward credential into OAuth provenance with its scopes, `assemble-execution-context.ts:419` puts `oauthScopes` on the envelope, and `admittingCredentialKind` tests `oauthScopes` FIRST. Tried to break it: the forward resolves through an established session, which would read `session` if the order were reversed or if `onAdmission` fired; it does not fire (`:298`, `forwardAgent ? undefined`), and an empty scope array is still an array. If the provenance is dropped (banned subject, user mismatch) there is neither `oauthScopes` nor an admission, and the key is absent.
- `credential` absent ⇒ "anything but `'session'`, absence included, as not that session". Holds and is the right default: every path that leaves the key absent (a host that skipped the identity step, a dropped forward provenance) is one where no session was proven, and the contract sends each to refusal.
- `impersonatedBy` absent ⇒ "the user in `id` is acting themselves". Holds within its stated reach, and only when read together with `credential`: an administrator's impersonation session always carries `session.impersonatedBy` off the same read that admitted it, cookie or bearer; every other way of acting as the user (their API key, an agent forward) is told apart by `credential`, not by this key. The contract says both halves, and the door needs both. A door that tested `impersonatedBy` alone would admit an API key; the `credential` docblock closes that in its own last sentence.
- "never the authorization subject, and no platform middleware reads it". Holds: the readers in the tree are attribution writers (plugin-audit, plugin-approvals, the engine's provenance plumbing), none of them a gate.
- Shape against `EvalUser` and `ActorUser`: the seven re-declared keys carry the types `ActorUser` declares, and `Type Check · workspace`, `· source gates` and `· consumer gates` are green on the head, so the `extends EvalUser` narrowing and the runtime assignment both compile.

`packages/runtime/src/domains/ai.ts`, sentence by sentence against the contract:

- `credential` comes from `admittingCredentialKind(context)`, the same function and the same `context` object the membership gate reads, so the route cannot disagree with the gate. Agrees.
- `impersonatedBy` comes from `ec.impersonatedBy`; `id` is untouched. Agrees.
- Both keys are omitted, never `undefined` (conditional spreads). Agrees with "Absent", and the test asserts it with `in`.
- `user` stays `undefined` when `ec.userId` is falsy, before either key is computed. Agrees.

`packages/runtime/src/security/admitting-credential.ts`: the alias and its docblock agree with the contract; the function body is unchanged.

Check-runs on the head: 56 success, 13 skipped, 2 failure (both `Check Changeset`, judged in ②). `Test Core` (8/8 shards), `Type Check · workspace`, `Spec property liveness`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard` and `Lint · PM dispatch-gates` are green.

Nits (none affects correctness or what a consumer may rely on; each is left as an accepted deviation or a follow-up card, since a fix on this face moves the head):

- N1 (nit) — `AIRouteUser` docblock: "absent for an anonymous caller (reachable only on a route that declares `auth: false`)". True for every caller the HTTP identity step resolves (it always sets `isSystem: false`, and `shouldDenyAnonymous` refuses the rest). `handleAIRequest` also leaves `user` absent for an in-process context with `isSystem: true` and no `userId`, on any route; that caller is not anonymous and the sentence does not name it. A door that treats absence as refusal is unaffected. The two older comments in `ai.ts` that say "only reachable when the deployment does NOT require auth" are stale on `main` and not this PR's.
- N2 (nit) — `impersonatedBy` is described as "carried as is"; `ai.ts` trims it and drops a blank. Core already trims at the source (`resolve-authz-context.ts:693`), so on the dispatcher path the value is identical; the difference shows only for a host that hands in its own padded context.
- N3 (nit) — the `oauth` bullet says both forms "resolve to an agent principal carrying the token's scopes"; `apiForwardAgentOf`'s own docblock allows an OAuth caller the MCP door did not resolve to an agent (a token naming no client). Unreachable on an AI route, where `oauth` arrives by the forward alone, which is minted only for a resolved agent. Together with the `ActorUser` key-set duplication in ③, one follow-up card would cover both: derive runtime's `ActorUser` keys from the spec type, and tighten the sentence.

Landing · PR #34736 (card #34184) · head `16f04a5fbd` · 2026-11-17T14:10Z

- Records: L1 full ACCEPT 6949485711 and contract review PASS 6949621570, both at `30f7347d`. `16f04a5f` is a clean merge of `origin/main` on top of it (K was 42), with no regenerated path, so both records carry over.
- `check-governed-merges.mjs --pr 34736`: NOT governed (361 lines). No Tier H.
- CI at `16f04a5f`: 57 success, 11 skipped. The one red is `Check Changeset`, on the declared DELIBERATE CORRECTION of `.changeset/33808-ai-door-confirmation-in-app.md` (ruling 6942875153, Q1 A). The L1 ACCEPT and the same-head contract PASS confirm it, and the check is not required (ruleset 12119582).
- Nits only remain (L1 N1, contract review N1–N3). By the maintainer's small-flaw rule (2026-11-17 12:44Z, 「只对 nit 级采用」) they are carried by #34849, which is knocked to triage.
- Readied and auto-merge armed in this stroke.

### ⛔ merge queue 构建失败 — 先分诊，再决定要不要重排

队列构建 [44100385301](https://github.com/objectstack-ai/objectstack/actions/runs/44100385301) 红了。队列跑的是**全量**套件（PR 侧 CI 只跑 affected 子集），
所以失败的测试可能在本 PR 没碰过的包里 —— 那不是重排能修的。每次盲目重排都会让排在后面的所有 PR 重建一轮。
